From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-29T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + proposed POC scope

Hi Samir 1

Thanks again for taking the time today 1 really useful conversation. Wanted to capture the key pain points and propose a short POC scope so we can align on success criteria and next steps.

Pain points you described:
- High latency and cost variability on current vendor endpoints for customer-facing chat (esp. peak usage)
- Lack of reliable token-level cost visibility across routes and models
- Risk of regression when switching model variants (quality drift on slot-filling prompts)

Customer goals for the POC (what success looks like):
1) Latency: median generation latency < 200ms p95 under a 50 RPS test workload
2) Cost: 30% reduction in per-token cost vs current baseline (measured on identical prompt sets)
3) Quality: no >5% drop in accuracy on the feature extraction prompt set (we'll use your labeled evals)
4) Operational: ability to route by region and fallback to a lower-cost model without user-visible errors

Proposed POC scope (4 weeks):
- Week 0: Access + environment setup (service account, API keys, test dataset)
- Week 1: Ingest prompt set + baseline runs (your current provider + Redwood recommended config)
- Week 2: Optimizations (batching, caching, quantization profile) + intermediate metrics
- Week 3: Final eval, handoff, and runbook + cost/latency report

Owners (Redwood): Marissa (AE, overall), Aditya (Solutions Engineer), Rishi (CS/ops).
Owners (Acme): Samir (product lead), Priya (ML ops), John (security contact).

Immediate asks from you:
1) Confirm the test prompt set (you mentioned ~2k prompts + 200 labeled evals)
2) Provide a service account or SSO access for the test environment (instructions below)
3) Share any security questionnaire items we should prep (SOC2 evidence, network controls)

Access/setup steps (high level):
- We’ll provision a temporary Redwood project and issue scoped API keys (we support IP allowlists and VPC peering for Private; for the POC we recommend API keys + allowlist)
- Provide a service account email or create a testing user and share SSO link; we’ll request minimal scopes
- We’ll share a Google Drive folder for prompt sets and results and invite your team

I’ve attached a one-page POC plan and a checklist (redwood-poc-plan.xlsx). If that looks good I’ll send calendar invites and loop in Rishi for the ops kickoff.

Thanks 1 talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

- On logs: for the POC we default to ephemeral logs retained for 30 days; we can provide a bucket export for your SOC team and remove logs at the end of the engagement per your policy. We’ll confirm exact retention in the kickoff.
- I reviewed your SOC questions and assigned Rishi to handle the evidence and the network/data flow diagram.

Proposed kickoff: Tuesday 2028-08-31 at 11:00am PT 1 45 minutes. Agenda: introductions, access checklist, confirm prompt sets & evals, baseline schedule, and immediate action items. I’ll send a calendar invite after you confirm.

POC success metrics (finalized for the kickoff):
- Latency: median <200ms, p95 under 350ms on 50RPS synthetic test
- Cost delta: target >=30% cost reduction on production prompt mix
- Quality: <5% drop on labeled evals; we’ll run rouge/accuracy and a small human review set
- Observability: token-level breakdown + per-route dashboard live in Redwood Console

Immediate Redwood action items (before kickoff):
1) Aditya: prep baseline runner + templates for hosted vs quantized runs
2) Rishi: gather SOC2 evidence pointers and prepare data flow diagram draft
3) Marissa: share Drive folder and HubSpot deal link

I’ve added the Drive link to the metadata for the thread and will send the invite as soon as Samir confirms.

Thanks 1 looking forward to it.
